entities.summary: Engelbert Dollfuss was an Austrian politician and dictator who served as chancellor of Austria between 1932 and 1934. Having served as Minister for Forests and Agriculture, he ascended to Federal Chancellor in 1932 in the midst of a crisis for the conservative and nationalist government. This crisis culminated in the self-elimination of the Austrian Parliament, a coup sparked by the resignation of the presiding officers of the National Council. Suppressing the Socialist movement in the Austrian Civil War and later banning the Austrian Nazi Party, he cemented his rule through the First of May Constitution in 1934.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Engelbert Dollfuss's rule had significant regional impact in Western Europe, particularly in Austria, where he suppressed the Socialist movement and banned the Austrian Nazi Party. His tenure also led to the establishment of the First of May Constitution in 1934.
